title: Hours are the same on the lines, confirmation, document and report
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with two labor lines of 1.5 and 0.75 hours.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. Open the Finance tab.
  5. Open Reports > Internal Work Orders.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The lines read 1.5 and 0.75 hours.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation reads "Labor 2.25 h".

Step 3:

  • The work order is Closed.

Step 4:

  • The document reads "Labor hours 2.25".

Step 5:

  • Work order 1's row reads Hours 2.25.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • Terminology: “Hours → the labor hours on the lines of the work order, as the document shows them. The Close confirmation, the NO CHARGE document and the Internal Work Orders report use them. Clocked hours per technician are in Technician Efficiency.”
  • S3-R2: “Close opens the confirmation "Close work order [number]?" with a posting date field (default today; it follows the rules of Invoice Date on the Finance-tab Create invoice today, and it is the date of the internal invoice, of every entry, and of the record in every report, export and the asset Invoices tab) and these rows: "Stock parts $[stock parts cost]" with the note "Posted to [mapped account name]" (the amount reads "$[amount], includes $[core amount] core cost" when a picked part carries a core, S2-E7); "Special orders and sublet $[amount]", one line per state present: already posted to the work order's account (note "Already posted to [account] at the vendor bill"), posted elsewhere and reclassed at Close (note "Moved from [account] to [account]"), and not yet billed (note "Posts to [account] when the vendor bill is entered"); the amount is the vendor bill line amount for billed items and the line cost for items not yet billed; the row is hidden when there are none; "Labor [hours] h" with the note "Hours only, nothing posted"; "Shop supplies $[amount]" with the note "Posted to [work order's expense account], credited to [shop supplies account]" (row hidden when the amount is $0.00). The document and the report show one Parts cost: stock parts plus special orders (S3-R5). Under the rows: "This posts the parts cost and shop supplies to your books and marks the work order Closed · Internal. You can reopen it later." when the work order is already Complete, or "This completes the work order, posts the parts cost and shop supplies to your books and marks it Closed · Internal. You can reopen it later." when it is not (Closed · No Charge on a no-charge work order). Buttons: Cancel and "Close Work Order". Parts cost is the cost on each line at Close, as invoicing posts to Cost of Parts today; the hours are the labor hours on the lines. With both QuickBooks and AccountingHub, each note names the QuickBooks account and the AccountingHub account. When the category requires the original work order and none was picked, the confirmation shows the select "Original work order *" (and "Original line") above the rows with the warning "[Category] requires the original work order. Pick the earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView."; Close Work Order stays disabled until one is picked; Goodwill never shows this. The Stock parts note names the category's account ("Posted to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense").”
  • S9-R2: “The report "Internal Work Orders" under Reports lists the closed internal and no-charge work orders of the organization and, one row each, the no-charge lines of invoiced billable work orders. Filters: date range on the posting or invoice date (default this month, at most 12 months), Location (all or one), Classification (All / Internal / No Charge / No Charge line), Category (All or one, archived under a heading), Original technician (All or one). Above the table a summary strip shows one card per category in the range: parts cost, count of work orders and lines, hours. Two tabs. "By work order and line", columns: Work order (link), Line ("Whole work order", or the line number and title), Customer, Classification, Category, Original work order (link, with the original line number when set), Original technician, Closed / invoiced (the posting date, or the invoice date for a line), Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, as on the NO CHARGE document, S3-R5; for a line, its own parts), Shop supplies (empty on a line), Hours (the labor hours on the lines, as on the document; clocked hours per technician are in Technician Efficiency with Only internal); a totals row for the whole range, not the page; rows sorted by date, newest first. "By technician", one row per technician with the columns Completed lines (lines with status Complete in the range on which the technician clocked time, the definition Technician Efficiency uses, so the two reports agree), Comeback lines and Warranty lines (no-charge lines of those categories whose stored original technicians include this technician, S2-R17), Comeback rate (comeback lines / completed lines), Redo hours and Redo parts cost (the hours and parts cost of that comeback and warranty work). A whole no-charge Comeback or Warranty work order counts as one line in this tab, with all its hours and parts cost. A line with several technicians counts once for each of them, in the numerator and the denominator, hours and cost shown whole for each; the totals row counts every line once; a note under the table says so. A row "Unassigned" holds the work without an original technician (Not in ShopView, or no technician on the original). The dollar cost of labor arrives with labor posting. Export: the PDF carries both tabs as sections with the same columns; the CSV carries the tab that is open, as every export gives what is on screen.”
